algorithm.title: Infertility initial evaluation algorithm

nodes.text: Infertility (> 12 months unprotected intercourse): perform semen analysis and evaluate ovulatory status
**Abnormal semen analysis:** refer male partner to reproductive urologist
**Irregular menses (anovulation):** measure TSH, prolactin, FSH, and assess for PCOS
**Regular menses + normal semen analysis:** perform hysterosalpingography to assess tubal patency
**Bilateral tubal occlusion on HSG:** offer in vitro fertilization (IVF) or tubal reconstructive surgery
**Normal HSG (unexplained infertility):** controlled ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination

c-obgyn-02-q048.hinge: Microcytic, hypochromic anemia (MCV 72, MCH 20) with normal hemoglobin A (95%) in pregnancy is iron deficiency anemia.
c-obgyn-02-q048.trap: African American ethnicity tempts sickle cell disease, but hemoglobin electrophoresis shows 95% hemoglobin A (normal adult hemoglobin).

A.fit: Not here: anemia is microcytic (MCV 72), not macrocytic

B.fit: Here: hemoglobin 10.2, MCV 72, normal electrophoresis

C.fit: Not here: produces normocytic indices, not microcytosis

D.fit: Not here: electrophoresis shows 95% hemoglobin A, no hemoglobin S

E.clue: Cobalamin deficiency causing macrocytic anemia and neuropathy
E.fit: Not here: microcytic indices, normal B12 absorption

algorithm.title: Evaluation of microcytic anemia in pregnancy

nodes.text: First-trimester anemia (hemoglobin < 11 g/dL) with low MCV (< 80 μm³): check serum ferritin
**Low serum ferritin (< 30 ng/mL):** diagnostic of iron deficiency anemia
**Normal or elevated ferritin:** perform hemoglobin electrophoresis to rule out hemoglobinopathies
**Elevated HbA2 (> 3.5%):** beta-thalassemia minor; partner genetic testing
**Normal electrophoresis with normal ferritin:** alpha-thalassemia trait (DNA testing)
Iron deficiency management: initiate oral elemental iron therapy daily with vitamin C to enhance absorption

c-obgyn-02-q049.trap: Donor egg conception at age 47 might tempt genetic testing (amniocentesis), but acute fundal enlargement requires immediate ultrasound evaluation.

nodes.text: Uterine size larger than dates (fundal height > 3 cm above expected): perform pelvic ultrasonography
**Multifetal gestation identified on ultrasound:** determine chorionicity and establish high-risk twin surveillance
**Inaccurate gestational age:** revise estimated due date based on early crown-rump length
**Uterine leiomyomas on ultrasound:** document size and location; monitor for degeneration pain
**Gestational trophoblastic disease (snowstorm pattern):** check quantitative β-hCG and perform suction curettage
Provide prenatal aneuploidy screening options based on donor oocyte age (32 years)

algorithm.title: Evaluation of postoperative cesarean fever and wound infection

nodes.text: Post-cesarean fever (POD 3-7): systematically examine lungs, incision, uterus, calves, and urine
**Incisional erythema, induration, and tenderness:** diagnose surgical site infection (wound infection)
**Superficial wound infection without fascial dehiscence:** open, debride, irrigate, and pack wound
**Systemic signs, cellulitis, or purulent drainage:** initiate broad-spectrum intravenous or oral antibiotics
**Fascial dehiscence or necrotizing fasciitis:** emergent surgical re-exploration and debridement in operating room
**Normal incision with exquisite uterine tenderness:** postpartum endometritis; start IV clindamycin + gentamicin

abnormal-uterine-bleeding.name: Abnormal uterine bleeding
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.scope: Adenomyosis, leiomyomas, endometrial polyps, ovulatory dysfunction, PALM-COEIN classification, endometrial biopsy
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.core: Abnormal uterine bleeding requires pregnancy exclusion, hemodynamic assessment and evaluation for structural disease or unopposed endometrial estrogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Perimenopause, PCOS, obesity, anticoagulants; lifelong heavy bleeding suggests inherited coagulopathy
Adenomyosis often multiparous; fibroids common during reproductive years

rows.label: Clues
items: Bleeding affecting quality of life, prolonged/heavy menses, intermenstrual or irregular bleeding
Tachycardia, orthostasis or syncope → clinically important blood loss
Postmenopausal bleeding requires malignancy evaluation even with a single episode

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PALM: Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia → structural causes
COEIN: Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not otherwise classified
Anovulation → absent cyclic progesterone, unopposed proliferation and unstable shedding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test and CBC** first; pelvic examination localizes uterine versus cervical/vaginal bleeding
**Transvaginal ultrasound** evaluates structural lesions; saline sonohysterography/hysteroscopy for intracavitary disease
★ **Endometrial biopsy ≥45 years**; younger with persistent bleeding, unopposed estrogen or failed treatment
Postmenopausal bleeding: endometrial thickness >4 mm → sampling; persistent bleeding → biopsy regardless of thickness
TSH for suspected endocrine disease; coagulation/vWF testing for suggestive bleeding history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → IV access, blood resuscitation, urgent gynecology; tamponade or operative control if needed
Stable acute heavy bleeding → high-dose combined OCP, progestin or tranexamic acid; estrogen contraindications matter
★ Long-term heavy bleeding → **levonorgestrel IUD**; combined OCP/progestin alternatives
Fibroids: symptom control, selected myomectomy/embolization; hysterectomy definitive when fertility no longer desired
Polyp → hysteroscopic removal; adenomyosis refractory to hormones → hysterectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency anemia; chronic anovulation → endometrial hyperplasia/cancer; structural lesions can impair fertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for chronic anovulation; replace iron and address metabolic drivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregnancy complication: positive hCG; exclude ectopic pregnancy
Cervicitis: friable cervix and postcoital bleeding

table.title: Structural clues
rows: Firm irregular enlarged uterus; pressure symptoms

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even when pregnancy reported unlikely; pelvic ultrasound assesses uterus and ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; high FSH + low estrogen → ovarian failure
Low/normal FSH + low estrogen → hypothalamic/pituitary cause; persistent unexplained prolactin elevation → pituitary MRI
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

amniotic-fluid-disorders.name: Amniotic fluid disorders
amniotic-fluid-disorders.scope: Oligohydramnios (AFI <= 5 cm or single deepest pocket < 2 cm, renal anomalies, uteroplacental insufficiency), polyhydramnios (AFI >= 24 cm, maternal diabetes, GI atresia, twin-twin transfusion syndrome, anencephaly)
amniotic-fluid-disorders.core: Amniotic fluid reflects fetal urine production and swallowing; abnormal volume directs evaluation toward membrane rupture, placental disease, or fetal anomalies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low fluid: PPROM, post-term pregnancy, maternal vascular disease, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs
High fluid: maternal diabetes, esophageal/duodenal atresia, anencephaly, fetal anemia; many mild cases idiopathic
Monochorionic twins: donor oligohydramnios and recipient polyhydramnios suggest twin-twin transfusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height smaller/larger than dates; fluid extremes may alter fetal movement perception
Severe excess → maternal dyspnea, distended tense abdomen; low volume → recurrent variable decelerations

rows.label: Pathophys
items: After midgestation, urine supplies most fluid; swallowing removes it
Placental hypoperfusion or absent kidneys reduces input; impaired swallowing or osmotic diuresis increases volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ultrasound fluid measurement** plus anatomy survey; single deepest pocket reduces oligohydramnios overdiagnosis
Low volume → sterile speculum examination for rupture, assess kidneys/bladder, growth and umbilical Doppler
High volume → diabetes testing, detailed fetal anatomy; evaluate anemia/infection when suggested

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Isolated persistent oligohydramnios → surveillance and delivery at **36–37+6 weeks**, or diagnosis thereafter
Low fluid from PPROM/FGR → manage underlying cause; intrapartum recurrent variables may benefit from amnioinfusion
★ Severe symptomatic polyhydramnios → **amnioreduction**; indomethacin not solely for fluid reduction
Mild idiopathic polyhydramnios → spontaneous term labor; elective induction no earlier than 39 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Early prolonged severe low fluid → pulmonary hypoplasia, limb contractures; later → cord compression
Excess fluid → preterm labor, malpresentation, prolapsed cord, abruption after decompression, postpartum atony

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize glucose control; avoid **ACE inhibitors** and nonessential NSAIDs during pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Macrosomia: large fundal height but normal fluid measurement
Incorrect dating: size discrepancy without true volume abnormality

amniotic-fluid-disorders.evidence: Polyhydramnios checked 2026-10-30: [SMFM Consult 46](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30048635/); oligohydramnios timing follows established ACOG guidance.

antepartum-fetal-surveillance.name: Antepartum fetal surveillance
antepartum-fetal-surveillance.scope: Nonstress test (reactive vs nonreactive), biophysical profile (BPP components and scoring), modified BPP, contraction stress test, umbilical artery Doppler, indications (FGR, diabetes, post-term, decreased movement)
antepartum-fetal-surveillance.core: Assess fetal well-being when stillbirth risk is elevated; abnormal screening generally needs confirmation or delivery according to gestation and severity.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ FGR, high-risk diabetes, hypertension, post-term pregnancy, decreased fetal movement

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Often around 32 weeks; earlier if severe risk and delivery would be considered
Decreased movement → prompt NST/fluid assessment; ongoing frequency based on underlying disorder

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Reactive NST ≥32 weeks: **two 15-beat accelerations lasting 15 seconds**, within 20 minutes
Before 32 weeks use 10 × 10; extend observation to 40 minutes for sleep
★ **BPP**: NST plus four ultrasound components; each 0 or 2, maximum 10

rows.label: IF positive
items: Nonreactive NST → stimulation/extended tracing, then BPP or selected contraction stress test
★ BPP ≤4 generally → delivery; 6 → repeat within 24 hours or term delivery
Low fluid requires evaluation despite score; umbilical Doppler guides FGR decisions

rows.label: Traps
items: BPP 8–10 reassuring only with normal fluid; modified BPP = NST + fluid assessment
CST: late decelerations with ≥50% contractions positive; avoid when labor contraindicated
False positives common; reassuring test does not predict acute abruption or cord accident

table.title: Ultrasound BPP: normal criteria during 30-minute observation

antepartum-fetal-surveillance.evidence: Indications checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG surveillance guidance](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2021/06/indications-for-outpatient-antenatal-fetal-surveillance); interpretation established obstetric teaching.

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; lactation and milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: painless postlactational mass; fat–fluid level on imaging
Abscess: focal tender erythematous fluctuant mass, sometimes fever; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → papilloma or malignancy evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Simple painful cyst → aspiration; bloody fluid or residual mass → further tissue evaluation
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID; galactocele → aspiration if symptomatic
★ Abscess → ultrasound-guided drainage + **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**; MRSA risk → clindamycin
Continue breastfeeding/pumping with lactational infection; persistent pathologic discharge → breast surgical evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

cervical-cancer-screening.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
cervical-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF guidelines by age (Pap smear alone 21-29, Pap with hrHPV cotesting or hrHPV alone 30-65), screening cessation, post-hysterectomy
cervical-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk people with a cervix from age 21; age, prior results, and cervical precancer history determine testing and cessation.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Average-risk cervix present**; sexual history and HPV vaccination do not alter schedule
HIV, immunosuppression, DES exposure, prior CIN 2+ → separate surveillance pathways

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Stop after 65 only with **adequate negative prior screening** and no high-risk history
Adequate: 3 negative cytology/2 HPV-based tests over 10 years; latest within 5
Total benign hysterectomy, no CIN 2+/cancer → stop; supracervical hysterectomy → continue

rows.label: Test
items: Choose one age-specific strategy below; annual testing increases unnecessary procedures

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ **HPV 16/18 or high-grade cytology → colposcopy**; other results use prior-history risk assessment
CIN 2+ treatment → HPV-based surveillance at least 25 years, even beyond 65

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Postcoital bleeding or visible lesion → diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening interval
Under 21: no routine screening; unknown/inadequate history after 65 → continue
USPSTF 2018 final schedule below; later draft self-collection proposals do not replace final guidance

table.title: USPSTF age-based choices
rows: Primary hrHPV or cotest every 5 years

cervical-cancer-screening.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF final recommendation (2018)](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/cervical-cancer-screening); post-treatment surveillance follows established ASCCP teaching.

cervical-neoplasia.name: Cervical neoplasia
cervical-neoplasia.scope: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, invasive cervical cancer, squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, colposcopy
cervical-neoplasia.core: Persistent high-risk HPV drives cervical precancer and cancer; abnormal screening needs risk-based evaluation, while visible symptomatic lesions require biopsy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV 16/18 persistence, smoking, HIV/immunosuppression, limited screening access

rows.label: Clues
items: CIN usually asymptomatic; invasive disease → postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding, watery discharge
Friable cervical mass, pelvic pain; hydronephrosis or leg edema suggests advanced spread

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral E6 degrades p53; E7 inactivates Rb → transformation-zone dysplasia
Squamous carcinoma most common; adenocarcinoma arises in endocervical glands

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Visible lesion → biopsy**, regardless of prior normal Pap/HPV result
★ HPV 16/18 positivity, ASC-H or AGC → **colposcopy**, even with otherwise reassuring screening
AGC → endocervical sampling; add endometrial biopsy at ≥35 or with endometrial risk factors
Colposcopy-directed biopsy diagnoses CIN; invasive cancer → pelvic examination, MRI/PET-CT for extent
Pregnancy → risk-based colposcopy; no endocervical curettage or expedited excision

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ CIN 3 → **excisional treatment** outside pregnancy; CIN 2 may be observed with fertility concerns
CIN 1 → observation; select nonpregnant patients ≥25 with very high risk → expedited excision
AIS → diagnostic excision; hysterectomy after childbearing if margins adequately assessed
Selected microinvasive cancer → conization; other early invasive disease → hysterectomy
Locally advanced → cisplatin-based chemoradiation plus brachytherapy

rows.label: Complications
items: Ureteral obstruction, fistulas, metastases; cervical excision increases subsequent preterm-birth risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **HPV vaccination** plus age-based screening; vaccination does not eliminate screening
After treated CIN 2/3/AIS: initial intensive HPV surveillance, then every 3 years for ≥25 years

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: mucopurulent discharge and positive STI testing
Endometrial cancer: uterine-source bleeding; benign ectropion: smooth eversion without destructive lesion

table.title: Histologic grade
rows: More than two-thirds; basement membrane intact

cervicitis-pid.name: Cervicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease
cervicitis-pid.core: Sexually active patient with mucopurulent discharge or postcoital bleeding; ascending infection adds pelvic pain, sometimes an adnexal abscess.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condoms, prior STI
IUD-associated PID risk concentrated within first 3 weeks after insertion

rows.label: Clues
items: Cervical friability, easily induced endocervical bleeding; infection sometimes asymptomatic
Dyspareunia, fever; severe unilateral pain/adnexal mass → **tubo-ovarian abscess**
Peritonitis, shock → rupture; RUQ pain → Fitz-Hugh–Curtis perihepatitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: GC/CT ascend cervix → endometrium/tubes; PID often polymicrobial, including anaerobes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** first; vaginal/cervical or urine **GC/CT NAAT**; HIV/syphilis testing
★ Pelvic pain + **cervical motion, uterine, OR adnexal tenderness** → presumptive PID; no confirmation delay
Negative cervical NAAT does not exclude upper-tract infection; normal discharge/no vaginal leukocytes argues against PID
**Transvaginal US** for abscess or diagnostic uncertainty; routine laparoscopy unnecessary

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Cervicitis: empiric GC/CT coverage IF high risk/unreliable follow-up; otherwise await NAAT
★ Admit IF **pregnant, abscess, severe illness**, oral intolerance, uncertain surgical diagnosis, or failure by 72 h
Abscess rupture → emergency surgery; persistent abscess after 48–72 h antibiotics → drainage
Pregnant chlamydia → **azithromycin**, avoid doxycycline; retain IUD initially, reassess if no improvement

rows.label: Complications
items: Tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; abscess → sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from prior **60 days**; abstain until courses completed, partners treated, symptoms resolved
Retest GC/CT at 3 months; pregnant chlamydia → test of cure at 4 weeks
Annual GC/CT screening: sexually active women <25, older women with risks; condoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, no confirmed intrauterine pregnancy
Ovarian torsion: abrupt unilateral pain, vomiting; Doppler flow may persist
Appendicitis: migrating RLQ pain, CT appendiceal inflammation

table.title: Antibiotic branches
rows: Ceftriaxone; add CT regimen unless excluded
Oral drugs 14 days; ceftriaxone once IM outpatient

chancroid.name: Chancroid
chancroid.scope: Haemophilus ducreyi, painful genital ulcers with ragged undermined margins, painful fluctuant inguinal lymphadenitis (bubo), azithromycin, ceftriaxone, differentiation from syphilis and herpes
chancroid.core: Painful, friable genital ulcers with ragged undermined edges and tender suppurative inguinal nodes suggest Haemophilus ducreyi infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure in endemic regions/outbreaks, multiple partners, inconsistent condom use
HIV and lack of circumcision associated with slower healing and treatment failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonindurated ulcer base, purulent exudate, easy contact bleeding; often multiple lesions
Buboes commonly unilateral; lymph-node suppuration may cause draining sinus tracts
Systemic symptoms usually limited; generalized rash or neurologic findings suggest another infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gram-negative coccobacillus enters mucosal breaks, producing local necrosis and regional lymphatic infection
Ulceration increases HIV acquisition and transmission risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical suspicion plus exclusion of **syphilis and HSV**; test all genital ulcers
Ulcer HSV NAAT and syphilis serology; very early negative syphilis result requires repeat testing
H. ducreyi culture needs special media, limited sensitivity; NAAT availability limited
★ Obtain **HIV test**; consider repeat testing/PrEP according to ongoing exposure risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Azithromycin orally once** or **ceftriaxone IM once**
Fluctuant buboes → needle aspiration or incision/drainage plus antibiotics
★ Reexamine in **3–7 days**; symptoms should improve before complete ulcer healing
No response → reassess diagnosis, adherence, coinfection, HIV, or antimicrobial resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Genital scarring, phimosis, fistulas, secondary infection; prolonged open lesions facilitate HIV spread

rows.label: Prevention
items: Condoms, abstain until lesions healed and partners treated
Examine/treat partners exposed during 10 days before symptom onset, even without symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless, indurated chancre with nontender nodes
HSV: grouped vesicles evolve into shallow ulcers; burning prodrome, recurrent episodes
LGV: small transient often painless lesion, later inguinal adenopathy or proctitis

chlamydia-infection.name: Chlamydia infection
chlamydia-infection.scope: Chlamydia trachomatis, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, NAAT screening and diagnosis, doxycycline and azithromycin
chlamydia-infection.core: Often silent sexually transmitted intracellular infection causing urethritis or cervicitis; untreated infection threatens fertility and can infect newborns during delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 years, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condom use, infected partner; perinatal exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, scant discharge, sterile pyuria; friable cervix, mucopurulent discharge, postcoital bleeding
★ Neonatal conjunctivitis at **5–12 days**; afebrile staccato pneumonia at **1–3 months**
LGV: transient painless genital ulcer → tender inguinal nodes/buboes or invasive proctocolitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: C. trachomatis: obligate intracellular bacterium; D–K serovars cause genital/perinatal infection, L1–L3 cause LGV

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT**: vaginal swab preferred in women; first-catch urine in men; rectal swab after exposure
Test for gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis; fever/pelvic pain → evaluate for PID
Infant conjunctival testing requires epithelial cells; nasopharyngeal testing for pneumonia
Sexually active MSM: annual site-specific screening; every 3–6 months with persistent high risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated infection → **doxycycline for 7 days**; LGV → 21 days
★ Pregnancy → **azithromycin**, single dose; alternative when adherence doubtful, less reliable for rectal infection
Neonatal disease → oral erythromycin for 14 days; azithromycin alternative; topical treatment alone inadequate
Gonorrhea suspected or detected → add ceftriaxone; PID requires broader multidrug coverage

rows.label: Complications
items: PID → tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; epididymitis, reactive arthritis
LGV → rectal strictures/fistulas; infant macrolides → hypertrophic pyloric stenosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; expedited partner treatment where legal
Abstain until 7-day course completed or 7 days after single dose, and partners treated
Annual screening: sexually active women <25 years, older women with risk; pregnancy entry screening, risk-based rescreening
Retest at 3 months; pregnancy test-of-cure at 4 weeks; neonatal eye ointment does not prevent chlamydia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gonorrhea: often more purulent; organism-specific NAAT differentiates
M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge

congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.core: Newborn salt loss or atypical genitalia demands adrenal evaluation; hypertension with abnormal puberty suggests a different steroid-synthesis block.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive inheritance; affected sibling, consanguinity
Classic disease presents neonatally; partial enzyme deficiency may present with adolescent androgen excess

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Neonatal vomiting, weight loss, dehydration, **shock** → salt-wasting adrenal crisis
46,XX virilization with internal female organs; 46,XY infants may lack obvious external warning signs
Nonclassic 21-hydroxylase deficiency: premature pubarche, hirsutism, acne or irregular menses

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Low cortisol removes feedback → ↑ACTH and adrenal hyperplasia
Steroid precursors accumulate upstream; androgen and mineralocorticoid effects depend on enzyme block

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **17-hydroxyprogesterone** screens for 21-hydroxylase deficiency; elevated values → confirmatory steroid testing
Borderline nonclassic disease → ACTH-stimulated 17-OHP; electrolytes, renin, cortisol and androgens guide subtype
Ambiguous genitalia → karyotype, pelvic ultrasound, endocrine consultation; avoid premature sex assignment
Newborn screen may miss milder disease; clinical instability overrides screening results

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crisis → **IV hydrocortisone**, isotonic saline, dextrose; treat severe hyperkalemia
Glucocorticoid replacement suppresses ACTH; salt-wasting forms → fludrocortisone plus infant salt supplementation
11β/17α-associated hypertension → glucocorticoids; add antihypertensives for persistent elevation
Genital differences → multidisciplinary counseling; timing of surgery requires informed shared decisions

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated crisis → death; androgen excess → precocious pseudopuberty, advanced bone age, short adult height
Excess replacement → growth suppression, obesity, osteoporosis; inadequate replacement → infertility/adrenal rest tumors

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Newborn screening, genetic counseling; emergency steroid kit, medical alert, illness/surgery stress dosing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen insensitivity: 46,XY, testes, absent uterus, normal adrenal steroids
Pyloric stenosis: vomiting with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis rather than salt-wasting hyperkalemia

congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

congenital-infections.name: Congenital infections
congenital-infections.scope: Cytomegalovirus (sensorineural hearing loss, periventricular calcifications), Toxoplasmosis (chorioretinitis), Parvovirus B19 (hydrops), Rubella, Varicella, Zika, screening and diagnosis
congenital-infections.core: Congenital infection causes growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or hydrops; organ-specific patterns identify the pathogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CMV: toddler saliva/urine; toxoplasma: undercooked meat, cat feces; B19: child with slapped-cheek rash
Absent rubella/varicella immunity; mosquito exposure or sexual transmission in Zika-risk areas

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae/blueberry-muffin lesions, abnormal fetal ultrasound; many infected newborns initially appear well
★ B19 hydrops: cardiomegaly, ascites, edema without red-cell alloantibodies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transplacental infection disrupts organogenesis; later exposure may cause inflammation or marrow suppression
Toxoplasma transmission increases with gestational age; earlier infection causes more severe injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal exposure → pathogen-specific **IgG/IgM**, paired titers or avidity; isolated IgM needs confirmation
★ CMV newborn diagnosis: saliva PCR then confirm urine PCR **within 21 days**
Suspected fetal infection → targeted ultrasound, pathogen-specific amniotic-fluid PCR; B19 → serial MCA Doppler
Prenatal rubella IgG routinely; no universal US maternal CMV, toxoplasma, or B19 screening

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic congenital CMV → **valganciclovir**, monitor CBC and liver tests
Congenital toxoplasmosis → pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin; maternal regimen depends on fetal infection
B19 severe fetal anemia → intrauterine transfusion; rubella/Zika structural injury → supportive care
Maternal varicella exposure without immunity → varicella-zoster immune globulin; maternal pneumonia → IV acyclovir

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, neurodevelopmental disability; delayed/progressive hearing loss requires longitudinal audiology

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Rubella/varicella vaccination before pregnancy or postpartum; **live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy**
Handwashing after diapers; cook meat, avoid litter handling; mosquito precautions and Zika exposure counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aneuploidy: abnormal genetic testing rather than pathogen testing
Rh disease: positive maternal antibody screen with fetal anemia

table.title: Discriminating congenital patterns
rows: Periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss
Severe microcephaly, subcortical calcifications, ocular abnormalities

congenital-infections.evidence: CMV testing checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cytomegalovirus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html); remaining pathogen patterns established teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; implants/IUDs provide years of protection; replacement interval depends on product
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel pills sooner preferred

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only method or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, thrombophilia/high-risk VTE**, severe hypertension, early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity; copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

disorders-of-sex-development.name: Disorders of sex development
disorders-of-sex-development.scope: 46,XY DSD (androgen insensitivity, 5-alpha-reductase deficiency), 46,XX DSD (congenital adrenal hyperplasia), mixed gonadal dysgenesis, ambiguous genitalia, pubertal virilization, karyotyping
disorders-of-sex-development.core: Atypical genital development requires urgent exclusion of salt-wasting CAH, then coordinated chromosomal, hormonal, and anatomic assessment with family-centered counseling.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, consanguinity, inherited steroid/receptor defects; maternal androgen exposure can virilize 46,XX fetuses

rows.label: Clues
items: Atypical genitalia, bilateral nonpalpable gonads, severe hypospadias with undescended testes, primary amenorrhea
★ Vomiting, weight loss, hypotension, **hyponatremia/hyperkalemia** in newborn → salt-wasting crisis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Testicular AMH regresses Müllerian ducts; testosterone supports Wolffian ducts; DHT masculinizes external genitalia
21-hydroxylase deficiency diverts precursors toward androgens while reducing cortisol ± aldosterone

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Electrolytes, glucose, 17-hydroxyprogesterone**, cortisol; salt-wasting may emerge after initially normal examination
★ **Karyotype/rapid sex-chromosome testing + pelvic ultrasound** for uterus and gonads
Testosterone, DHT, LH/FSH, AMH; high testosterone:DHT ratio after hCG supports 5-alpha-reductase deficiency
Confirm with targeted molecular testing; involve pediatric endocrinology, genetics, urology, psychology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected adrenal crisis → **IV hydrocortisone + isotonic saline/dextrose**, without awaiting confirmatory results
Salt-wasting CAH maintenance: hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone, salt supplementation in infancy
Complete AIS: discuss gonadectomy after spontaneous puberty; individualize surveillance; estrogen replacement after removal
Mixed dysgenesis with Y-containing dysgenetic gonads → specialist malignancy-risk assessment, often gonadectomy
Avoid rushed irreversible genital procedures; informed shared decisions include option to defer until patient participation

rows.label: Complications
items: Adrenal crisis, infertility, gonadal tumors, psychosocial distress; hormone deficiency affects bone health

rows.label: Prevention
items: Newborn CAH screening, genetic counseling; educate affected families about stress-dose steroids and emergency injections

rows.label: Mimics
items: Müllerian agenesis: 46,XX, absent uterus, normal pubic hair and ovaries
Isolated hypospadias: typical endocrine function; severe proximal forms still warrant DSD evaluation

table.title: Distinguishing profiles
rows: Undervirilized at birth, virilizes at puberty

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after starting/changing drugs**, then every 6–12 months; assess adherence
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG now omits routine testing/prophylaxis before 12 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue

endometrial-cancer.name: Endometrial cancer
endometrial-cancer.scope: Endometrial hyperplasia, endometrioid adenocarcinoma, uterine sarcoma (leiomyosarcoma, carcinosarcoma, radiation risk), unopposed estrogen, biopsy, staging
endometrial-cancer.core: Postmenopausal bleeding warrants endometrial evaluation; chronic unopposed estrogen drives hyperplasia and endometrioid carcinoma.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, chronic anovulation/PCOS, nulliparity, early menarche, late menopause, estrogen without progestin
Tamoxifen, Lynch syndrome; prior pelvic radiation increases uterine sarcoma risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Abnormal uterine bleeding, watery/bloody discharge; pelvic pain or enlarged uterus with advanced disease
Growing postmenopausal uterine mass → consider sarcoma; growth rate alone cannot establish malignancy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Atypical hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia: premalignant lesion with frequent concurrent carcinoma
Serous/clear-cell cancers: aggressive, estrogen-independent; carcinosarcoma classified as high-grade carcinoma
Leiomyosarcoma: malignant myometrial smooth muscle, usually de novo rather than transformation of benign leiomyoma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AUB at **≥45 years**, or younger with persistent bleeding/estrogen risks → endometrial biopsy
★ ACOG 2026: most postmenopausal bleeding → **TVUS plus tissue sampling**
Classic ≤4 mm reassurance rule changed; persistent bleeding always requires histology, regardless of thickness
Insufficient/negative blind biopsy with continued symptoms → hysteroscopy-directed biopsy; Pap does not exclude disease
Surgical staging assesses myometrial/cervical invasion, nodes, extrauterine spread; sarcoma can escape endometrial sampling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Operable carcinoma → **total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy**, sentinel-node assessment
Advanced/high-risk disease → stage-directed radiation and systemic treatment; carboplatin/paclitaxel commonly used
Suspected sarcoma → intact uterine removal; avoid uncontained morcellation

rows.label: Complications
items: Anemia, metastasis, recurrence; lymph-node surgery → lymphedema

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Weight management; add **progestin to systemic estrogen** when uterus intact; evaluate Lynch families

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginal atrophy: thin friable mucosa; malignancy still needs exclusion
Leiomyoma: usually premenopausal, well-circumscribed smooth-muscle mass

table.title: Hyperplasia
rows: Progestin, often levonorgestrel IUD; repeat sampling
Hysterectomy; selected fertility preservation: progestin + serial biopsies

endometrial-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG bleeding update 2026](https://www.acog.org/news/news-releases/2026/04/acog-publishes-updated-guidance-evaluation-postmenopausal-bleeding), [EIN consensus](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/clinical-consensus/articles/2023/09/management-of-endometrial-intraepithelial-neoplasia-or-atypical-endometrial-hyperplasia); other content established teaching.

endometriosis.name: Endometriosis
endometriosis.scope: Pelvic endometriosis, deep infiltrating endometriosis, endometrioma (chocolate cyst), uterosacral nodularity, cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, laparoscopy, medical management
endometriosis.core: Reproductive-age patient with progressive cyclic pelvic pain, deep dyspareunia, and infertility from ectopic endometrial tissue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, short cycles, prolonged menstruation, family history; obstructed menstrual outflow

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Uterosacral nodularity**, fixed retroverted uterus, posterior cul-de-sac tenderness
Dyschezia or cyclic rectal bleeding → bowel involvement; urinary cyclic symptoms → bladder disease
Pain severity poorly correlates with lesion burden; examination may be normal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Estrogen-responsive implants provoke inflammation, fibrosis, adhesions, and distortion of pelvic anatomy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical assessment + **transvaginal ultrasound** first; normal imaging cannot exclude superficial disease
MRI maps deep lesions or indeterminate adnexal masses; CA-125 not a diagnostic test
★ **Laparoscopy with biopsy** for uncertain diagnosis, refractory symptoms, or planned operative treatment
Current ACOG approach supports presumptive clinical diagnosis; surgery not required before empiric treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain, no immediate pregnancy goal → **NSAID + continuous combined OCP** or progestin
Persistent symptoms → GnRH agonist/antagonist with add-back hormones to limit hypoestrogenic adverse effects
Refractory disease or selected infertility → laparoscopic excision/ablation and adhesiolysis
Endometrioma surgery may reduce ovarian reserve; balance pain, suspicion, size, and fertility goals
Trying to conceive → fertility evaluation; hormonal suppression does not improve spontaneous conception

rows.label: Complications
items: Adhesive infertility, bowel/ureteral obstruction, chronic pain; small increase in clear-cell/endometrioid ovarian cancer
GnRH suppression → hot flashes, bone loss; disease may recur after conservative surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Postoperative hormonal suppression reduces pain recurrence when pregnancy not desired; no established primary prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adenomyosis: diffusely enlarged, boggy uterus with heavy bleeding
PID: fever, discharge, cervical motion tenderness; pain less cyclic
Primary dysmenorrhea: normal examination, onset soon after menarche, no structural lesion

table.title: Anatomic forms
rows: Fibrotic nodules involving ligaments, bowel, bladder
Ovarian chocolate cyst; homogeneous ground-glass ultrasound echoes

fetal-growth-restriction.name: Fetal growth restriction
fetal-growth-restriction.scope: Symmetric vs asymmetric FGR, uteroplacental insufficiency, chromosomal anomalies, congenital infections, umbilical artery Doppler surveillance, oligohydramnios
fetal-growth-restriction.core: Estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile requires evaluation for placental dysfunction and fetal disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal hypertension, preeclampsia, renal/vascular disease, smoking, cocaine, malnutrition, prior affected pregnancy
Aneuploidy, structural anomalies, CMV; multiple gestation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height lag >3 cm, decreased movement, oligohydramnios; sometimes abnormal maternal placental disease markers
★ **EFW <3rd percentile** indicates severe disease; normal-size parents do not establish constitutional smallness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental resistance reduces oxygen/nutrients; redistribution preserves cerebral over abdominal growth
Low fetal renal perfusion reduces urine production and fluid volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ultrasound biometry using reliable dating → detailed anatomy; serial growth generally every 3–4 weeks
★ **Umbilical artery Doppler every 1–2 weeks**; absent (AEDV)/reversed (REDV) diastolic velocity → intensified surveillance
Weekly NST after viability; increase frequency with Doppler deterioration or maternal comorbidity
Early <32 weeks, unexplained or anomalous → offer amniocentesis/microarray; CMV PCR if amniocentesis chosen
Do not order indiscriminate TORCH panels without exposure or suggestive findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reversed flow → **hospitalization**, corticosteroids, frequent cardiotocography, delivery planning
Anticipated preterm birth → betamethasone; magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection before 32 weeks
Nonreassuring testing/maternal deterioration → earlier delivery; absent/reversed flow may favor cesarean
Bed rest, sildenafil, and LMWH solely to treat/prevent FGR provide no established benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, intrapartum intolerance, neonatal hypoglycemia, hypothermia, polycythemia; later metabolic/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tobacco/drug cessation, maternal disease control; low-dose aspirin when preeclampsia-risk criteria met

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates: early ultrasound establishes gestational age
Constitutionally small fetus: reassuring interval growth and normal Doppler without placental disease

table.title: Patterns and delivery in otherwise stable disease
rows: Often later placental insufficiency; patterns overlap

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities

group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.name: Group B streptococcus prophylaxis
group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.scope: Universal rectovaginal screening (36-37 weeks), intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis indications (prior infant with GBS, bacteriuria, unknown status with fever, ROM >=18h, <37 weeks), IV penicillin G, penicillin allergy
group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.core: Intrapartum antibiotics reduce early-onset neonatal GBS disease in colonized patients and those with specified obstetric risk factors.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All pregnancies: culture; prior affected infant or current **GBS bacteriuria** → automatic prophylaxis

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Screen **36+0–37+6 weeks**; result generally valid 5 weeks
Begin antibiotics at labor or membrane rupture; aim ≥4 hours exposure without delaying delivery

rows.label: Test
items: **Rectovaginal culture**; request clindamycin susceptibility with serious penicillin allergy

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Positive culture → **IV penicillin G**; ampicillin acceptable
Unknown status + <37 weeks, temperature ≥38°C, or ROM ≥18 hours → prophylaxis
Suspected intra-amniotic infection → broad-spectrum antibiotics including GBS coverage

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Planned prelabor cesarean with **intact membranes** → no GBS prophylaxis, regardless of culture
GBS bacteriuria ≥100,000 CFU/mL or symptomatic UTI also needs antepartum treatment
Antepartum eradication of asymptomatic vaginal colonization does not replace intrapartum antibiotics

human-papillomavirus-infection.name: Human papillomavirus infection
human-papillomavirus-infection.scope: Low-risk HPV and condyloma, high-risk oncogenic HPV (16, 18), anogenital intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinomas, HPV vaccination
human-papillomavirus-infection.core: Most HPV infections clear spontaneously; persistent oncogenic infection causes precancer, while low-risk types cause anogenital warts.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual skin-to-skin contact, new/multiple partners, immunosuppression, HIV
Smoking promotes persistent infection and cervical neoplasia; penetration not required for transmission

rows.label: Clues
items: Condyloma acuminata: painless flesh-colored, verrucous or cauliflower-like genital/perianal growths
High-risk infection usually asymptomatic; postcoital bleeding or abnormal cervical lesion needs diagnostic assessment
★ **Ulceration, induration, fixation, pigmentation, bleeding**, or nonresponse → biopsy rather than empiric retreatment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **HPV 6/11** mainly cause warts; **16/18** account for major oncogenic risk
High-risk E6/E7 interfere with p53/Rb → dysplasia and invasive carcinoma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical external warts → **visual diagnosis**; HPV testing does not guide wart management
Biopsy atypical lesions or uncertain diagnosis, especially with immunosuppression
Cervical HPV/cytology screens for neoplasia; abnormal results → risk-based colposcopy and directed biopsy
No routine HPV screening of asymptomatic partners or blood testing for infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Warts: **imiquimod, podofilox, cryotherapy**, or trichloroacetic acid; choose by site, burden, pregnancy
Pregnancy: avoid podofilox/podophyllin; use clinician-applied cryotherapy or acid when treatment needed
High-grade intraepithelial lesions → site-specific ablation/excision; visible suspicious cancer → biopsy and staging
Treatment removes lesions without reliably eradicating virus; asymptomatic infection needs no antiviral

rows.label: Complications
items: Cervical, anal, vulvar, vaginal, penile, and oropharyngeal carcinomas; recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
Warts frequently recur; treatment may cause local irritation, ulceration, pigment change

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **9-valent vaccine before exposure**; catch-up through 26 years, shared decision at 27–45 years
AAP: two doses starting <15 years; three if older/immunocompromised; federal 2026 policy differs
Vaccinated people still need cervical screening; condoms reduce but do not eliminate transmission

rows.label: Mimics
items: Condyloma lata: broad moist flat secondary-syphilis lesions, positive serology
Molluscum: smooth umbilicated papules; skin tags: soft pedunculated growths

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.scope: Definition (failure to conceive after 12 months), initial evaluation, semen analysis (male factor), ovulatory status (midluteal progesterone), tubal and uterine factors (hysterosalpingography), ovarian reserve testing
infertility.core: No conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; evaluate after 6 months at age ≥35, immediately over 40 or with risks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, PCOS, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemotherapy, testicular injury, exogenous testosterone
Smoking, marked weight extremes, premature ovarian insufficiency, untreated endocrine disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/absent cycles → ovulatory dysfunction; galactorrhea → hyperprolactinemia; hot flashes → ovarian insufficiency
Prior ectopic pregnancy or chlamydia → tubal damage; normal cycles do not exclude male factor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failure of sperm production/delivery, oocyte release, fertilization, transport, or implantation; mixed factors common

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Evaluate **both partners simultaneously**; reproductive history, sexual timing, examinations; semen analysis early
Abnormal semen result → repeat and male reproductive evaluation; do not begin with female laparoscopy
★ Ovulation uncertain → **progesterone about 7 days before expected menses**; >3 ng/mL supports ovulation
Regular 21–35-day cycles usually imply ovulation; targeted TSH, prolactin only for relevant symptoms
★ **HSG** for tubal patency; saline sonography for cavity; avoid HSG during pregnancy/infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ PCOS anovulation → **letrozole**; hyperprolactinemia → cabergoline; correct thyroid disease
Tubal occlusion/severe male factor → IVF, sometimes intracytoplasmic sperm injection
Unexplained infertility → ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination, then IVF if unsuccessful
Intercourse every 1–2 days during fertile window; avoid testosterone for fertility-seeking men

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; stimulation → ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple gestation; assisted reproduction → ectopic pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: STI prevention, tobacco cessation, weight optimization; fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment
Preconception folic acid and medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infrequent intercourse: inadequate exposure despite normal reproductive testing
Recurrent pregnancy loss: conception occurs, followed by repeated losses

table.title: Ovarian reserve: treatment response, not natural fertility
rows: Low values suggest reduced follicular pool

infertility.evidence: Evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2021](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/); treatment established reproductive guidance.

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate, reason, communicate choice**; specific to decision, fluctuating
Competence: legal determination; diagnosis, age, or disagreement alone does not establish incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, including life-saving treatment; avoid coercion or abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no available surrogate/directive → implied consent for necessary treatment
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or substantially changed risk → renewed consent discussion

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

intra-amniotic-infection.name: Intra-amniotic infection
intra-amniotic-infection.scope: Chorioamnionitis, clinical diagnostic criteria (maternal fever, fetal tachycardia, purulent fluid, uterine tenderness), IV ampicillin and gentamicin, labor augmentation, postpartum endometritis
intra-amniotic-infection.core: Intrapartum fever with fetal tachycardia or purulent cervical drainage suggests ascending infection requiring antibiotics and delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged membrane rupture, prolonged labor, repeated digital examinations after rupture, internal monitoring
Genital tract colonization; infection can occur with intact membranes

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterine tenderness, foul amniotic fluid, maternal tachycardia, leukocytosis
Hypotension, altered mentation, oliguria → maternal sepsis; leukocytosis alone nonspecific during labor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Polymicrobial ascent from vagina into decidua, membranes, amniotic fluid, and fetus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected infection: temperature **≥39°C**, or **38–38.9°C plus one additional clinical risk factor**
Additional factors: fetal baseline >160/min, purulent cervical drainage, maternal leukocytosis without corticosteroids
ACOG 2024 permits diagnosis without fever when other clinical findings strongly support infection
Clinical diagnosis; placental histology or amniotic-fluid testing confirms retrospectively; never delay treatment
Sepsis → blood cultures, lactate, CBC, renal function; cultures before antibiotics only without delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Prompt **IV ampicillin + gentamicin**, acetaminophen, IV fluids; notify neonatal team
★ Induce/augment labor with **oxytocin**; infection alone is not a cesarean indication
Cesarean for obstetric indication → add clindamycin for anaerobic coverage; postpartum dosing depends on course
Shock → fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine, urgent source control; do not await fetal lung maturity

rows.label: Complications
items: Uterine atony/hemorrhage, postpartum endometritis, bacteremia, septic shock
Neonatal pneumonia, sepsis, meningitis; prematurity-related morbidity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Minimize digital examinations after rupture; timely term-PROM induction; PPROM latency antibiotics when expectant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epidural-associated fever: sterile inflammation possible; cannot dismiss coexisting infection
★ Postpartum endometritis: fever and fundal tenderness after birth → **clindamycin + gentamicin**
Pyelonephritis: flank tenderness and positive urine culture

intra-amniotic-infection.evidence: Diagnostic update checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG 2024](https://doi.org/10.1097/aog.0000000000005593); management follows established ACOG teaching.

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes, averaged over 30 minutes

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Sustained bradycardia → vaginal examination for prolapsed cord; prepare urgent delivery

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV with relatively preserved hemoglobin and high RBC count suggests thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

multiple-gestation.name: Multiple gestation
multiple-gestation.scope: Dichorionic diamniotic (lambda sign), monochorionic diamniotic (T-sign), monochorionic monoamniotic, twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS), selective FGR, delivery timing recommendations
multiple-gestation.core: Chorionicity and amnionicity determine twin-specific surveillance, complications, and delivery timing; establish both on first-trimester ultrasound.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dizygotic twins: ovulation induction/assisted reproduction, maternal age, family history
Monozygotic splitting timing determines placental and sac sharing

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterus larger than dates, exaggerated pregnancy symptoms; ultrasound confirms fetal number
★ Shared placenta with **oligohydramnios/polyhydramnios sequence** → TTTS; small/absent donor bladder
Selective FGR: one small twin, discordant estimated weights; assess each umbilical artery Doppler

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental vascular anastomoses permit imbalanced flow in monochorionic twins
Donor hypovolemia reduces urine; recipient hypervolemia increases urine and cardiac strain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **First-trimester ultrasound** identifies shared placenta and intertwin membrane
Monochorionic diamniotic → ultrasound **every 2 weeks from 16 weeks** for fluid/bladders
Serial growth in all twins; Doppler and more frequent assessment when growth discordance develops
TTTS donor deepest pocket ≤2 cm, recipient ≥8 cm; staging incorporates bladder, Doppler, hydrops

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ TTTS stages II–IV at 16–26 weeks → **fetoscopic laser ablation** of placental anastomoses
Asymptomatic stage I → at least weekly surveillance; refer fetal intervention center if progression/symptoms
★ Diamniotic twins with **first twin cephalic** may deliver vaginally with experienced team
Monoamniotic twins → cesarean; fetal deterioration, preeclampsia, or severe growth issues may require earlier delivery

rows.label: Complications
items: Preterm birth, preeclampsia, anemia, gestational diabetes, postpartum hemorrhage
Monoamniotic cord entanglement; monochorionic co-twin death can cause surviving twin neurologic injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention; optimize iron/nutrition; single-embryo transfer reduces iatrogenic multiples

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates/macrosomia: enlarged uterus but singleton on imaging
Twin anemia-polycythemia sequence: discordant MCA velocities without major fluid imbalance

normal-and-abnormal-labor.name: Normal and abnormal labor
normal-and-abnormal-labor.scope: Latent vs active first stage, second stage, active phase protraction and arrest (oxytocin, cesarean), false labor (Braxton Hicks), operative vaginal delivery, labor induction
normal-and-abnormal-labor.core: True labor produces progressive cervical change; dystocia management depends on stage, contraction adequacy, fetal status, and descent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Nulliparity, obesity, fetal macrosomia, malposition, cephalopelvic disproportion, inadequate uterine contractions

rows.label: Clues
items: Assess membrane status, presentation, fetal heart tracing, serial dilation, station, and maternal vital signs
★ Tachysystole: **>5 contractions/10 minutes**, averaged over 30 minutes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysfunctional powers, passenger, or passage → delayed dilation or descent

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active arrest requires ruptured membranes: no change after **4 hours adequate** or 6 hours inadequate contractions
Adequate activity: ≥200 Montevideo units; intrauterine pressure catheter when external assessment insufficient
Prolonged pushing: >3 hours nulliparous, >2 hours multiparous; individualize by descent and fetal status
Failed induction requires ≥12–18 hours oxytocin after ROM; slow latent phase alone does not mandate cesarean

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Protraction with weak contractions → **oxytocin**, amniotomy; established active arrest → cesarean
Tachysystole → stop oxytocin, lateral positioning; persistent fetal compromise → terbutaline, expedited delivery
★ Operative vaginal birth requires full dilation, ruptured membranes, engaged head, known position, skilled operator
Unfavorable cervix → balloon or prostaglandin ripening, then oxytocin; avoid misoprostol after prior cesarean
Avoid vacuum before 34 weeks or with face presentation; failed operative attempt → cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal infection, hemorrhage, exhaustion; neonatal hypoxia
Forceps/vacuum → maternal lacerations, neonatal scalp injury; vacuum → subgaleal hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Induce for maternal/fetal indications or offer elective induction from 39 weeks; no elective earlier delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: irregular contractions without cervical change
Obstructed labor: adequate contractions without progress; augmentation cannot correct mechanical obstruction

ovarian-torsion.name: Ovarian torsion
ovarian-torsion.scope: Ovarian cyst, ovarian torsion, Doppler ultrasonography, detorsion, cystectomy
ovarian-torsion.core: Abrupt unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and vomiting suggests twisting of the adnexal vascular pedicle, requiring rapid ovarian-preserving surgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovarian cyst/mass, especially >5 cm; pregnancy, ovulation induction, prior torsion
Functional cysts and mature teratomas common lead points; adolescents may torsion a normal ovary

rows.label: Clues
items: Intermittent severe pain from twisting/untwisting; adnexal tenderness or mass; mild leukocytosis possible
Fever, guarding, peritoneal findings may indicate advanced ischemia; absence does not reassure
Pregnancy test can be positive with torsion; pregnancy does not establish ectopic implantation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Venous/lymphatic outflow obstruction → congestion and edema, followed by reduced arterial inflow
Dual arterial supply may preserve detectable flow despite clinically important vascular compromise

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; assess shock, competing surgical diagnoses
★ **Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler** first; transvaginal when feasible, transabdominal in younger adolescents
Enlarged edematous ovary, peripheral follicles, free fluid, twisted pedicle support diagnosis
★ **Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion**; no laboratory test reliably rules it out
High clinical suspicion → diagnostic laparoscopy; no serial imaging delay to prove loss of flow

rows.label: Tx
items: NPO, IV access, fluids for dehydration, analgesia/antiemetic; urgent gynecology consultation
★ **Laparoscopic detorsion with ovarian preservation**, even if dark/blue appearance
Cystectomy if safely feasible; friable edematous ovary → defer cyst removal and reassess
Oophorectomy only if unavoidable tissue destruction or compelling malignancy concern; avoid removal for color alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Ovarian infarction, diminished ovarian reserve, infertility, recurrent torsion
Unnecessary extensive resection sacrifices viable ovarian tissue; timely treatment maximizes salvage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Residual cyst → **ultrasound at 6–12 weeks**; persistent significant cyst may need elective cystectomy
Ovulation suppression may reduce recurrent functional cysts; oophoropexy individualized after recurrent torsion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine gestation or concerning pregnancy-location evaluation
Ruptured hemorrhagic cyst: abrupt pain with free fluid; often improves without persistent torsion signs
PID: discharge, cervical motion tenderness, STI risk; bilateral symptoms more typical

pelvic-organ-prolapse.name: Pelvic organ prolapse
pelvic-organ-prolapse.scope: Anterior compartment (cystocele), posterior compartment (rectocele, enterocele), apical compartment (uterine prolapse, vaginal vault prolapse, procidentia), pelvic floor muscle training, pessary, surgical repair
pelvic-organ-prolapse.core: Loss of pelvic support causes a vaginal bulge with pressure, urinary symptoms, or obstructed defecation, often worse when standing or straining.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vaginal births, increasing age, menopause, obesity, connective-tissue weakness
Chronic cough/constipation, heavy lifting; hysterectomy predisposes to vaginal vault descent

rows.label: Clues
items: Visible/palpable protrusion, incomplete bladder emptying, stress leakage, need to splint vagina for defecation
★ **Urinary retention or hydronephrosis** with advanced descent → evaluate obstruction promptly
Symptoms improve supine; mucosal rubbing can produce spotting or ulceration

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Levator ani injury and fascial/ligamentous failure permit descent of one or several vaginal compartments

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pelvic examination during Valsalva**, sometimes standing; isolate compartments with speculum
POP-Q stages descent relative to hymen; measure postvoid residual when voiding symptoms present
Urinalysis for urinary symptoms; creatinine/renal ultrasound when severe obstruction suspected
Reduce prolapse during cough stress testing to unmask occult stress incontinence before surgery

rows.label: Tx
